context: Hex-binned US population density map using 20,000 synthetic GPS points around major cities, rendered on canvas with a sequential Tol color scale and an interactive radius slider.
first_impression: Structurally honest design — color encodes count with a data-driven 0-to-maxCount domain — but the screenshot shows an empty map (external resource load failure), and a 32-bucket color quantization step introduces minor encoding approximation.
what_works: Color domain is fully data-driven via d3.max(bins, d => d.length) and recalculates on every radius change; legend correctly anchors at 0 and maxCount with intermediate midpoint label.
what_doesnt: The 32-bucket quantization assigns representative rather than exact colors to each bin (bucket midpoint approximation), so bins near bucket boundaries render with a slightly wrong hue; the screenshot captured an empty render, indicating fragility when external CDN resources (us-atlas, d3-hexbin) fail to load before screenshot time.
